Expands NVIDIA Partnership For AI Packaging Capacity

The companies plan to boost advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, aiming to increase interposer wafer capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028.

The agreement brings the companies’ multi-year agreements in South Korea and Arizona to a combined $3 billion, supporting rising demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.

The investments will help align Amkor’s manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans as advanced packaging becomes increasingly important for performance, power efficiency and chip integration.

Amkor CEO Kevin Engel said the expansion strengthens the company’s global manufacturing footprint and its ability to serve customers in the U.S. and South Korea.

  • The conference call was very bullish and caused SPCX stock to spike.

    • SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said AI computing investments are currently paying back in less than a year, with the possibility of a six month payback next year.  These are extraordinary economics for a capital intensive business.
    • SpaceX is targeting approximately 13 gigawatts of AI computing capacity by the end of 2027, up from just 1.7 gigawatts at the end of September.  Musk even raised the possibility of exceeding 20 gigawatts.
  • The character of the stock market regarding AI in this phase is changing from the prior phase.  SpaceX earnings provide another important data point.  In the prior phase of AI in the stock market, investors rewarded companies for announcing massive AI spending.  In this phase, investors are beginning to demand evidence of returns on that spending.
  • Further in our analysis, SpaceX is showing extraordinary returns on AI computing today.  However, its own plans to dramatically increase capacity illustrate the risk.  As more capacity comes online across the industry, competition could pressure computing prices and reduce returns.  This is a hidden risk that prudent investors need to pay attention to. 
  • Also in our analysis, the bottleneck is also changing.  Having the best chips is no longer enough.  Connectivity, power, cooling, and the ability to bring computing capacity online quickly are becoming increasingly important competitive advantages.
    • In this phase of AI, investors will need greater differentiation between winners and losers.
    • Expect sharp swings in stock prices.

President Donald Trump will highlight his administration’s crackdown on overseas crypto scam networks at a White House event Wednesday.

What the Crackdown Actually Involves

A White House official told Reuters that Trump and cabinet members, including Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel and Attorney General Todd Blanche, will showcase seizures of fraudulent crypto investment websites and efforts to stop online impersonation scams.

Recent enforcement numbers back that focus up:

  • Oct. 13: the Justice Department announced an international operation that led to 28 arrests in Ghana and Nigeria, removed more than 3.7 million scam-linked accounts and pages, and identified over $11 million in potentially freezable funds, with Coinbase, Binance, Meta, Google and Microsoft all taking part.
  • Brooklyn prosecutors separately disrupted 241 scam domains tied to a multinational crypto scheme targeting Russian speakers, seizing 112 servers in the process
  • Scam Center Strike Force: a broader effort has now restrained roughly $938 million in crypto, including $52 million restrained in a single day in September alone

The scale of the underlying problem dwarfs those recoveries. FinCEN identified $12.7 billion in suspected scam-related financial activity across more than 33,000 reports filed between September 2023 and December 2025. 

The FBI separately reported Americans filed over 1 million internet crime complaints in 2025, with crypto investment fraud accounting for more than $7.2 billion of those losses.

Why Trump’s Own Crypto Ties Complicate the Message

A Reuters investigation found Trump and his sons added at least $2.3 billion to their family fortune through crypto ventures, while investors who bought in lost roughly the same amount.

World Liberty Financial (CRYPTO: WLFI) contributed the largest share, directing more than $1.4 billion in token sales to the family, while the TRUMP (CRYPTO: TRUMP) meme coin brought in about $616 million for them against more than $700 million in investor losses.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Reuters that “all actions by President Trump and his administration are taken in the best interest of the American people.”

Benzinga previously reported that U.S. authorities sanctioned two men tied to a World Liberty-linked resort project in East Timor during a separate crackdown on overseas scam networks. World Liberty said it had no knowledge of or relationship with either individual.

Trump also pardoned Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in October 2025, after Zhao’s company pleaded guilty to failing to maintain anti-money laundering controls. 

He signed a March executive order directing the DOJ to prioritize prosecuting online scammers, then later tasked the Department of Homeland Security with working alongside private companies to track foreign hacking groups.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) heads into third-quarter earnings with investors balancing strong AI-driven advertising momentum and early enthusiasm around Muse against heavy infrastructure spending, enterprise restrictions and questions over when the new AI agent will meaningfully contribute to revenue.

Meta shares gained more than 2% Wednesday after falling almost 4% over the previous five sessions, as investors repositioned ahead of the company’s Oct. 21 earnings report.

Wall Street expects third-quarter earnings of $5.74 per share, down from $7.25 a year earlier, while revenue is projected to rise to $63.37 billion from $51.24 billion.

BNP Paribas Sees Muse Upside and Execution Risk

BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones maintained a positive view with an $885 price forecast.

Jones said Muse continues to gain downloads while maintaining solid retention. He sees long-term opportunities in transaction fees, data insights, increased engagement across Meta’s Family of Apps and advertising.

However, he flagged growing restrictions from companies in e-commerce, banking, insurance, travel and media that are limiting Muse’s access over security concerns.

Jones said those restrictions show Meta still needs to refine Muse’s product-market fit and work with content and commerce partners rather than disintermediate them.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Rosenblatt Expects Strong Ad Growth

Rosenblatt Securities analyst Barton Crockett maintained a Buy rating and an $886 price forecast.

He expects third-quarter revenue growth near the upper end of Meta’s 19%-25% guidance range, supported by AI-driven improvements in engagement and ad effectiveness.

Rosenblatt projects revenue of $63.94 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.95.

Crockett expects Meta to spend $130 billion-$145 billion on capital expenditures in 2026 and said a move toward roughly $200 billion in 2027 would be reasonable. He believes core advertising improvements can justify those investments even before Muse becomes a meaningful revenue contributor.

Citizens Sees a Large Long-Term Opportunity

Citizens JMP Securities analyst Andrew Boone maintained a Market Outperform rating and an $885 price forecast.

Boone expects consumer AI agents to surpass 100 million daily active users by the end of 2027 and estimates Muse could generate more than $10 billion in annual advertising revenue at that scale.

That potential is not included in his current forecasts.

He sees advertising as the stronger monetization model for AI agents as they increasingly help users discover products, complete tasks and make purchases.

Together, the analysts remain bullish on Meta’s AI opportunity, but the near-term debate centers on capital intensity, enterprise adoption and how quickly Muse can translate usage into sustainable revenue.

SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion. Its Super Intelligence unit, formerly the AI division, brought in $7.56 billion, up 830%.

• SpaceX stock is showing exceptional strength. What’s behind SPCX gains?

The company guided first-quarter 2027 revenue to $33 billion to $37 billion, against Wall Street estimates near $23 billion.

SpaceX’s gain was its biggest one-day move since Aug. 7, when the stock climbed 15.8%, and added roughly $200 billion in market value in a single session. JPMorgan more than doubled its price target to $500 from $240.

(NASDAQ:NFLX) fell 5% even though third-quarter adjusted EPS of 87 cents beat the 82-cent estimate, as fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $13.4 billion came in just below the $13.5 billion consensus. TD Cowen

The firm lifted revenue and EBITDA estimates by an average of 21% and 26% a year from 2026 through 2031. TD Cowen now expects SpaceX to finish 2026 with 2.7 gigawatts of terrestrial compute capacity, up from 2.1 GW, and to reach 8.5 GW in 2027.

Blackledge highlighted CFO Bret Johnsen’s comment on pricing, which is running slightly above the top of last quarter’s $30 to $50 per watt range. New deployments could pay for themselves in under a year. 

SpaceX can "capitalize on a significant and arguably unprecedented market opportunity" in Super Intelligence and space, he wrote.

Yorkville Ives & Co.

Analyst Dan Ives kept an Outperform rating and a $225 target on SpaceX. His attention went to a potential merger with Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA). 

CEO Elon Musk said both companies have formed special committees of independent directors, and he cannot take part in their talks. Any deal would need approval from 50% of all Tesla shares, a bar Musk called high.

Ives is not worried. "We believe there is an 80%-90% chance that Tesla and SpaceX merge by the end of 2027 for a number of strategic AI and data-driven reasons and this is the right move for Musk," he wrote. He also pointed to a $63 billion backlog, with about $42 billion expected to be recognized within a year.

Cantor Fitzgerald

Cantor analyst Colin Canfield reiterated an Overweight rating, raised his target to $345 from $246 and made SpaceX his top coverage pick. 

The firm boosted its 2027 Intelligence sales estimate to roughly $260 billion from about $40 billion. Cantor now models more than 10 GW of terrestrial compute by the end of 2027, compared with roughly 4 GW before, and sees the company turning free cash flow positive by 2028.

Canfield said he expects SpaceX shares "to massively outperform tomorrow." His prediction came true with SPCX shares up 9.83% at $162.33 on Wednesday afternoon, according to Benzinga Pro market data.

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is buying billions in Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) AI hardware, but some new server racks are sitting in warehouses because its data centers lack the electricity to run them, Business Insider reported Tuesday.

Internal emails show Amazon expected to receive $5 billion worth of Nvidia AI server systems in August, followed by another $3 billion a month. The company did not specify how long those purchases would continue.

Amazon Buys Before It Can Plug In

Amazon introduced an “Early Rack Receipt” program to secure Nvidia chips amid fierce competition, even before its data centers are ready.

Previously, Amazon waited until the equipment arrived at its data centers before taking ownership. Now it pays earlier, even if the servers have to sit in warehouses waiting for electricity.

Some sites have space for the racks but insufficient power, Business Insider reported. One supply-chain team didn’t know when the Nvidia servers it was receiving would actually be installed and ready to use.

Amazon called staging hardware near deployment sites “best business practice” and disputed suggestions that AWS lacked a broader deployment plan.

The Cost of Waiting

At a September internal meeting, AWS CFO John Felton joked to infrastructure chief Prasad Kalyanaraman, according to a separate Business Insider investigation:

“You’ve taken us free cash flow negative as a company, so congratulations.”

Kalyanaraman described Amazon’s AI business as “hugely free cash flow negative” and expected the company’s free cash flow to remain negative for another couple of years.

Amazon plans $220 billion in company-wide capital spending this year. Free cash flow fell to negative $7.6 billion for the 12 months ended June 30, from positive $18.2 billion a year earlier.

Unpowered servers cannot earn revenue, while delays may shorten the period before newer chips make them less competitive.

AI Bubble Odds Rise

Noted AI skeptic Ed Zitron estimated in September that $200 billion to $300 billion worth of AI chips could be sitting in warehouses or unpowered data centers because companies are buying hardware faster than they can put it to work.

Business Insider’s findings at Amazon provide concrete evidence of the problem he described, although the value of Amazon’s unused equipment remains unknown.

Polymarket traders now see a 10% chance of an AI bubble burst by Dec. 31, up from 6% days earlier. Odds reach about 22% by June 30, 2027, though just $35,000 has traded on that contract.

A “Yes” requires three specified industry stress events within 90 days. Unpowered chips alone do not qualify.

Amazon Says Demand Is Real

AWS revenue rose 37% to $42.2 billion in the second quarter, while its backlog reached $496 billion.

Felton told Axios that AWS AI servers were achieving payback in under three years, arguing that demand justifies the spending.

Morgan Stanley has warned of a 32-gigawatt power shortfall facing U.S. data centers through 2028, raising questions about how quickly purchased hardware can start earning revenue.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA) stock slid 3% lower Wednesday as investors weighed the company’s aggressive AI expansion against persistent technical weakness, even as the broader U.S. market and consumer discretionary sector moved higher.

The Nasdaq gained 1.13%, the S&P 500 rose 0.44% and Consumer Discretionary advanced 0.20%, leaving Alibaba moving against the broader market.

• Alibaba stock is showing notable weakness. What’s behind BABA decline?

Alibaba Expands AI Computing Capacity

Alibaba remains focused on building artificial-intelligence capabilities across computing infrastructure, consumer hardware and its Qwen ecosystem.

The company joined other Chinese technology giants in placing more than $35 billion in combined orders for NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) RTX PRO 5500 chips, according to Reuters.

The orders underscore demand for additional AI computing capacity, although Nvidia has warned customers that supply may fall well short of Chinese demand.

Qwen Push Expands Into Wearables

Alibaba also expanded Qwen into consumer hardware with its Qwen Glasses N1 lineup and Qwen Clip earbuds, developed with Bose.

The devices support translation, meeting summaries, voice services and other AI-assisted tasks. The Pro glasses add health monitoring, eye tracking and iris verification.

Qwen Vice President Song Gang said, "The goal of Qwen is to become everyone’s Personal Agent."

The launch places Alibaba in closer competition with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in AI-powered smart glasses while extending Qwen deeper into Alibaba’s consumer ecosystem.

CEO Eddie Wu has positioned the company around a full-stack AI strategy spanning models, applications, chips, data centers and consumer devices.

China Market Volatility Adds Pressure

Alibaba shares also remain sensitive to broader swings in Chinese technology stocks.

Earlier in October, U.S.-listed Chinese stocks rallied amid speculation that authorities intervened to curb selling, although traders could not confirm the precise trigger.

Technical Trend Remains Bearish

Alibaba trades 4% below its 20-day SMA, 7.8% below its 50-day SMA, 8.1% below its 100-day SMA and 18.5% below its 200-day SMA.

The 20-day average remains below the 50-day average, while the Death Cross formed in April — when the 50-day SMA dropped below the 200-day SMA — continues to signal longer-term technical weakness.

Analysts Remain Bullish

Alibaba carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price target of $189.67.

JPMorgan maintained Overweight while lowering its forecast to $200 on Oct. 12. Citigroup maintained Buy and raised its forecast to $193 on Oct. 8, while Susquehanna maintained Positive and increased its forecast to $190 on Aug. 28.

news.content:
Anthropic PBC has signed up for more than $600 billion in long-term computing capacity, and its own draft IPO prospectus says the company still cannot get as much as it wants.

  • MSFT stock is moving with the AI trade. Get all of the details here. 

The numbers surfaced in a draft filing reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The draft prospectus details planned payments of $111 billion to Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), $110 billion to Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN) and $31 billion to Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) even if the company does not use all the computing capacity covered by those agreements.  

The hyperscalers are only part of the picture. Anthropic could pay as much as $86 billion to rent Nvidia-powered computing resources from providers Nscale and Lambda under agreements running through 2033 and 2034, respectively. Both providers deploy chips from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA). 

The long-term infrastructure tab could surpass $600 billion once obligations under a Google chip-leasing arrangement involving Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO), with Broadcom tied to more than $160 billion in leased Google chips.

Where the Filing Admits the Gap

The shortfall shows up in the prospectus risk disclosures. Anthropic warned that access to computing capacity remains uncertain, saying it has sought more capacity than some major cloud partners were willing to provide as they increasingly view Anthropic as a competitor.

Read plainly, the companies collecting the largest checks from Anthropic are also rationing supply to it. Google, Amazon and Microsoft each sell rival AI models or back competing labs.

Anthropic is also discussing additional agreements that could push its total commitments up by as much as $150 billion. If those deals are completed, the total could reach about $750 billion.

Read Also: Ken Griffin Calls AI a Bubble After Citadel Bought the Dip

Spending Already Running Hot

The red-hot demand for AI explains the urgency. Anthropic generated about $16.3 billion in revenue in the six months ended June 30, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, while spending on computing capacity and infrastructure climbed to nearly $9 billion, compared with $2.3 billion in the first half of 2025. 

The six-month total exceeded the $7.3 billion Anthropic spent on computing and infrastructure throughout 2025.

The losses look severe on paper. The vast majority of its $80.7 billion first-half loss, $72 billion, stemmed from accounting charges tied to changes in the value of convertible notes and other financial instruments issued to raise capital.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

An Overlooked AI Catalyst

Anthropic’s S-1 draft landed on a crowded day. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) drew most of the attention with its quarterly report, where its superintelligence segment posted revenue of $7.6 billion, driven by cloud services and the deployment of compute infrastructure.

Anthropic’s disclosure could arguably matter more for the broader AI trade. A buyer with $600 billion already committed, and openly asking for more, signals multi-year demand for chips, data centers and cloud capacity. Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia and Broadcom all sit on the receiving end.

Investors will get a closer look soon. The disclosures come as Anthropic prepares for a potentially blockbuster IPO that could value the company at as much as $2 trillion.

news.content:
Wall Street has found a new way to trade the rise of AI agents: buy the hotels, sell the websites that book them.

The bet is that software agents will book rooms straight from Marriott’s or Hilton’s own websites, leaving online travel agencies with less to do and fewer commissions to collect.

The charts are already moving that way.

Marriott International Inc. (NASDAQ:MAR) rose 1.7% to about $404 on Wednesday afternoon, a record high and on track for its 10th straight daily gain.

That is Marriott’s longest winning streak since an 11-session run that ended on Dec. 26, 2019. In price data going back to 1998, the stock has never risen more than 11 days in a row.

The 13.4% climb over those 10 sessions has added about $12.4 billion to Marriott’s market value.

Read Also: This 146-Old Can Maker Is On a Winning Streak Unseen In Its Half-Century Stock History

Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. (NYSE:HLT) has gained 9.7% over the past two months.

The middlemen are moving the other way. Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) has dropped 25.1% over the same two months, and Expedia Group Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) has lost 12.6%.

That leaves a gap of more than 38 percentage points between Marriott and Booking since late August.

Why AI Agents Threaten The Middlemen

Online travel agencies earn a commission because they save travelers time: one site, every hotel, prices side by side.

An AI agent does the same comparison on its own, in seconds, and can then go straight to the source.

Citrini Research turned that idea into a trade on Sept. 22.

In a report titled “Agentic Reality,” the firm pointed to Muse, the consumer agent from Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), whose free tier offers 100 million tokens a week.

Asked how it books flights, Muse told Citrini it uses a professional system that pulls inventory directly from airlines, not consumer sites such as Expedia or Kayak.

“The ultimate service provider – the hotel, airline, or rental car – still gets the customer,” Citrini wrote.

The firm picked four hotel companies for the long side: Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt Hotels Corp. (NYSE:H) and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts Inc. (NYSE:WH).

All four have gained at least 13% since the report. Booking has slipped, while Expedia is roughly flat.

Not Every Drop Is About AI

Most of Booking’s two-month decline came before the Citrini report, and regulators did part of the damage.

In September, a European court upheld the EU’s block of Booking’s 1.63 billion euro purchase of travel firm eTraveli. In early October, Reuters reported that Priceline faces Federal Trade Commission action over an affiliate’s hotel ads.

On Wednesday, the European Commission opened an investigation into Booking.com over phishing scams and fake listings. Booking shares fell 4.1% in afternoon trading.

Wall Street Is Not Convinced The Agencies Lose

BTIG kept a Buy rating and a $250 price target on Booking in late September, arguing that fears about AI agents may be overdone. “We argue agents will point travelers towards the OTAs,” the firm said, citing their breadth of supply and real-time pricing.

Morgan Stanley rates Booking Overweight with a $230 target. Its case rests on supply: Booking lists 4.7 million independent hotels and alternative stays, inventory no hotel chain can match.

“We see AI as both a new acquisition channel and a product opportunity, but execution will determine how much of the economics and consumer relationship the OTAs ultimately retain,” Morgan Stanley said in a Sept. 16 note.

Even Citrini’s own test left room for that view. Muse told the firm it still checks Booking.com for hotels, because prices can differ from the brand’s website.

Read Also: AI’s Most Watched Cooling Stock Has Fallen for 11 Straight Days: Analysts Now See a 50% Upside

There is also a new toll booth to watch. According to a Bank of America note published Oct. 16, Meta plans to charge a commission on purchases completed through Muse. Expedia is already among its partners.

The agent may not remove the middleman. It may become one.

Booking is building its own. On Oct. 14, it announced a planned $100 million investment in Vayo, an AI travel agent that tracks trips booked anywhere, including directly with hotels.

“A trip isn’t a task, and travelers deserve more than a chatbot,” said Mike Fridgen, Vayo’s chief executive and co-founder.

The Numbers Have Not Caught Up Yet

Hotel stocks are pricing a shift in how people book. The booking data proving it has not arrived.

Expedia reports third-quarter results on Nov. 4. Direct-booking share, marketing spend and any sign of agent-driven traffic will show whether the split on the charts shows up in the numbers.

Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META) reported financial results for the third quarter after the closing bell on Wednesday. Here’s a rundown of the report.

  • Meta Platforms stock is moving in positive territory. What’s driving META shares up?

Meta Q3 Earnings Highlights

Meta posted revenue of $64.6 billion for the quarter, beating analyst estimates of $63.37 billion. The tech giant reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share, beating estimates of $5.74 per share, according to Benzinga Pro.

Total revenue was up 26% on a year-over-year basis. Family daily active people increased 3% year-over-year. 

Ad impressions jumped 10% year-over-year and average price per ad increased by 14% year-over-year. Meta noted its headcount was down 15% year-over-year to 66,775 as of June 30.

Meta generated $32.79 billion in cash flow from operations and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion during the quarter. The company ended the period with $82.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.

“We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone — including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model,” said Mark Zuckerberg, founder and CEO of Meta Platforms. “Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we’re seeing velocity across the board.”

Meta expects fourth-quarter revenue to be in the range of $73 billion to $76 billion versus estimates of $73.74 billion.

Meta expects full-year 2026 expenses to be in the range of $175 billion to $179 billion, up from prior guidance of $165 billion to $169 billion. The increased guidance is due to a $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in the third quarter. The company anticipates full-year capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion versus prior guidance of $130 billion to $145 billion.

Meta also announced plans to establish a new class of common stock (Class C), effective January 2027. The company’s board declared a one-time stock dividend of one share of Class C common stock for each outstanding share held to be paid after the new class of common stock becomes effective, essentially acting as a two-for-one stock split.

Meta management will further discuss the quarter on an earnings call at 4:30 p.m. ET. A link to the call has been provided below.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) reported third-quarter financial results on Wednesday. The transcript from the company’s third-quarter earnings call has been provided below.

This transcript is brought to you by Benzinga APIs. For real-time access to our entire catalog, please visit https://www.benzinga.com/apis/ for a consultation.

View the webcast at https://events.q4inc.com/attendee/132342320

Summary

Meta Platforms reported a 26% increase in Q3 total revenue to $64.6 billion, driven by strong ad revenue and engagement metrics across Facebook, Instagram, and Threads.

The company highlighted the successful launch of the Muse personal agent, achieving over 10 million users in the US and Canada with strong engagement and retention metrics.

Meta is focused on scaling Muse globally, enhancing compute efficiency, and growing revenue through commerce tools and enterprise services.

Reality Labs experienced a 6% decline in revenue due to lower Quest headset sales, but the company expects improved profitability in 2027 with new product offerings and strategic adjustments.

Meta plans to create a new class of non-voting stock to enhance capital flexibility, indicating readiness for future investments in AI and other growth areas.

The company projects Q4 2026 revenue between $73 billion and $76 billion, with continued strong performance expected in 2027 from both core ads and emerging AI initiatives.

Full Transcript

Krista (Operator)

Good afternoon. My name is Krista, and I’ll be your conference operator today. At this time I would like to welcome everyone to Meta Platforms’ third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers’ remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star-one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star-one again.

We ask that you limit yourself to one question, and this call will be recorded. Thank you very much. Rob Bevegny, Meta’s Director of Investor Relations. You may begin.

Rob Bevegny (Director of Investor Relations)

Thank you. Good afternoon and welcome to Meta Platforms’ third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Joining me today to discuss our results are Mark Zuckerberg, CEO, and Susan Li, CFO. Our remarks today will include forward-looking statements which are based on assumptions as of today. Actual results may differ materially as a result of various factors, including those set forth in today’s earnings press release and in our quarterly report on Form 10-Q filed with the SEC.

We undertake no obligation to update any forward-looking statement. During this call we will present both GAAP and certain non-GAAP financial measures. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures is included in today’s earnings press release. The earnings press release and an accompanying investor presentation are available on our website at investor.appmeta.com. Now I’d like to turn the call over to Mark.

Mark Zuckerberg (Chief Executive Officer)

All right. Hey everyone, thanks for joining today. This has been a busy and exciting few months. Our family of apps is now used by 3.64 billion people each day, and we are seeing all-time highs in engagement on both Facebook and Instagram. Driven by strong growth in video, Threads has now overtaken X in monthly actives and continues to grow quickly. WhatsApp is hitting all-time highs in messaging and is becoming an increasingly important platform for agents as well.

In the last few months we have had several major milestones towards our goal of delivering personal superintelligence to everyone. We had one of our most successful launches ever with the Muse personal agent. We shipped Muse Wonder as our first frontier model, and we shipped several new glasses and gadgets with Muse integration, including coming soon to our new audio glasses. We’ve been discussing our vision for personal superintelligence for more than a year now.

We want to help every person have an extremely capable personal agent that understands your goals and can help you achieve them and improve your life in whatever ways you want. Whether that’s improving your relationships, helping you save time, save money, build a business, create new things, or anything else that you can dream of. Muse is the product form of this vision. So now we have the foundational technology in place to deliver this. There is still a lot of work ahead, but our initial position is very strong.

In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents. Growth continues to be strong and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day. Engagement and retention are also off to a strong start. About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on any given day. For our earliest adopters, the longer that they use Muse, the better that retention seems to get. So to put this in perspective, this is more than twice the level that Threads started at, or where we believe that other AI apps started at as well.

The most common use case for Muse is shopping, with more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this. With an average purchase size of over $200, Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before, and in the first week we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected. Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar.

Now this shows the importance of the Muse Secure VM that we’ve built to provide state-of-the-art privacy and security. And we are looking forward to following up soon with the Muse Confidential VM, which will make it so that even Meta cannot see your content. We’ve also seen that Muse Wonder improves quality, engagement, and retention further, which suggests that as we continue to improve intelligence, Muse will perform better and better over time.

Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it. The goals for this next phase play to many of Meta’s strengths. We need to do three things: scale the product, grow revenue, and optimize compute costs. We expect to grow Muse to serve billions of people. This is both our mission and our strategy. It’s our mission in that we believe in putting the power of personal superintelligence in everyone’s hands. We believe that that is the path to ensuring a positive future for everyone, with individual empowerment as the source of prosperity and balance of power as the foundation for safety. On a values level, we believe that delivering this capability widely is the best thing that we can be doing.

This is also our strategy because we think that billions of Muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together. So we’d like to create a large-scale Muse network as quickly as possible. From a business perspective, the average revenue per American user for our existing family of apps users is several hundreds of dollars annually, and we expect that Muse will reach an even higher level over time due to the amount of commerce that we already see taking place. This will take some time, but we’re starting to work on this now. Our business model will have a few components. For most people the product should be free and we will build commerce tools so we get paid a fee based on the transactions that we help facilitate.

We expect this will be paid for by businesses. For people who want the most advanced models or to use extra tokens, they subscribe directly and pay. For business owners who want additional features to use Muse to grow their businesses, or for companies that want people to use Muse for work, they will be able to subscribe directly and pay as well. And for those who want Muse to help improve the personalization and quality of their content and ads across Meta, they will be able to connect to those experiences as well.

Just to clarify, the average revenue that I was talking about before is the family of apps revenue for our existing Muse users. On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years. In the near term, Muse is very compute intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale. If compute efficiency continues improving quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years.

The strength of our core business enables us to scale the Muse network before then, and we believe that we are the best positioned company to pursue this strategy. One other note on compute economics is that since training is a large fixed cost, now that we have leading models, we want to serve as much high-margin inference demand as possible. That is why we are building the Meta Enterprise platform led by CJ Desai. Muse Wonder and even more advanced models that we’re training can serve additional high-margin services beyond the Muse network, including our API, Muse Code, and other enterprise services.

A fundamental feature of our business is that we have many good uses for this compute. It is difficult to forecast the exact growth rates for the Muse network, for our enterprise platform, and for how Muse Wonder and beyond will accelerate our core business. But through building up multiple ways to deploy these advanced models, we increase the chances that one or more of them significantly outperforms our expectations. Beyond serving other businesses, we have not yet found the limit of how effectively we can apply compute to accelerating our own core business. We have implemented an eval with Muse Wonder to improve how effectively it can autonomously improve our recommendations and ad systems. And as our upcoming models get even more advanced, I expect that we’re going to see an increasing rate of improvement in these systems.

All right, let’s talk about the models now. Muse Wonder is state of the art across many dimensions that matter for personal superintelligence. This validates the importance of training models ourselves to deliver the best experience. In addition to Muse, we have also seen that engagement per person in Meta AI has more than doubled since April when we started rolling out our new models. While Muse Wonder has been our most important release, I’ve been very pleased with our pace of execution here.

In the last few months, we’ve shipped MuseSpark 1.2 and 1.3, Muse Code 2 open-weights models with Muse Glimmer and MuseSpark Open, and also Muse Voice. Going forward, with the field advancing quickly, we plan to focus on both pushing the frontier of intelligence and distilling those models into much smaller and more efficient product models that will be optimized for personal agents. My view is that we will be able to build superintelligence through scaling, so we are methodically working our way up the ladder there.

We are already working on larger models after Muse Wonder, and they’re going to be very impressive and capable. We are also working on new smaller models that are coming out soon that will deliver Muse Wonder–level intelligence more efficiently. Moving on, our work on personal superintelligence is now also the focus of Reality Labs. Muse is coming to Meta Glasses starting next month and that will be an important step towards this. People already love many features of the glasses already: music, calling, capturing moments, hearing assistance, and more. But over time we expect Muse and having your personal superintelligence with you throughout the day will be the most important part of the experience.

Muse is also central to the business model for the glasses. Again, our mission and strategy are to serve everyone here. We believe in putting the power of this technology in everyone’s hands. So we have priced our devices not to make a large profit on the hardware, but to build a large software and superintelligence business on top of them. Now, we think that the most important thing that we can be building for this next generation of technology is basically putting the power of this technology in everyone’s hands, which is the personal superintelligence vision. So we’ve been working on this for a while. This is when we did the reboot around MSL and building the lab. A lot of it was this idea that we need to build models specifically to be good as personal agents, that we’d be able to build the best experience by owning and building and designing ourselves the end-to-end technology. I’d also say, you know, we have unique touch points to, again, you know, I mentioned in my opening remarks, 500 million self-identified small businesses.

And, you know, we think that many of the investments that we make in consumer products are going to carry over to help power those businesses. Also, we have multiple excellent channels to surface those opportunities to small businesses globally. Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) just put on a flying-car show, but "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O’Leary is looking past the stunt. He thinks the bigger story is a merger with Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), and he says shareholders of either company could end up owning both.

O’Leary Sees One Company 

O’Leary shared a video on X on Oct. 17 that he recorded with Meta (NASDAQ:META) smart glasses while visiting Thailand. He first talked through the practical problems of flying cars in cities, then turned to what Tesla’s latest Roadster demonstration means for investors.

"I think there’s no question that Tesla’s going to merge with SpaceX because that technology is coming together like this," O’Leary said.

He then laid out what that would mean for shareholders.

"So if you own Tesla stock, you’re going to own New Co," O’Leary said. "If you already own SpaceX, hang in. You’re going to own Tesla. It’s going to happen that way."

The Roadster Is a Sports Car With a Rocket Habit

His comments followed Tesla’s Oct. 15 demonstration of its long-delayed second-generation Roadster at SpaceX’s facility in Texas. An uncrewed prototype drove upside down up a ramp, launched into the air, performed midair flips and hopped over a lineup of Tesla vehicles before landing with the help of SpaceX-derived cold-gas thrusters.

Tesla also claimed a 0-to-60 mph time of 0.81 second during one run. Production is still targeted for 2028, though the most extreme thruster setups may not suit ordinary public roads.

The demonstration also put the overlap between the two companies on display. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has discussed collaboration across his businesses, including the proposed Terafab semiconductor project designed to support their growing computing needs. 

SpaceX has purchased Tesla Megapacks, Tesla has held SpaceX shares, and artificial intelligence chatbot Grok has been integrated into Tesla vehicles following SpaceX’s combination with xAI. The two companies also share interests in AI, computing infrastructure and advanced engineering.

Wall Street Is Already Doing the Merger Math

O’Leary is not the only one watching for a combination. Yorkville Ives Senior Managing Director Dan Ives has put the odds of a Tesla-SpaceX merger by the end of 2027 at 80%, pointing to the companies’ growing technological overlap and shared ambitions in AI.

Barclays analysts have also said a merger announcement could come before Tesla’s next annual shareholder meeting. The analysts said AI infrastructure and Musk’s desire to coordinate technology strategy across his companies could be motivations for a deal.

Any deal would raise questions about relative valuations, shareholder compensation and which company ends up acquiring the other. It would also need shareholder approval.

Crypto Market Gains Momentum

Bitcoin topped $84,000 but encountered strong resistance at $84,800. Ethereum also hit a wall in the early $2,500s, retreating to the $2,400 region.

Cryptocurrency-related stocks also fell, with Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ:MSTR) and Bitmine Immersion Technologies Inc. (NYSE:BMNR) closing up 7.54% and 5.04%, respectively.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency announced a final rule to implement the GENIUS Act, establishing requirements for permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the GENIUS Act “marks a watershed moment in American finance” and compared it to President Abraham Lincoln’s National Currency Act of 1863 that created a framework for a uniform national currency.

“Retail traders make up the vast majority of public commentary, and prices frequently move opposite their emotional extremes,” Santiment noted. “This is typical crypto behavior, where extreme crowd confidence and fear often arrive late.”
